result.note: Tests the April–June 2026 GDP composition, the JCRA sovereign rating upgrade and the six pillars of Semicon 2.0.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's GDP data for the April to June 2026 quarter, released in September 2026:
items: Growth of 7.8% exceeded the Reserve Bank's own estimate of 7% for the quarter.
Private investment growth closed at 12%, nearly doubling its pace.
Lending grew at its fastest pace in over a decade.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three are correct. The economy grew 7.8% against a 7% RBI estimate, private investment closed at 12% and lending grew at its fastest in over a decade. Investment leading growth rather than consumption points to a turn in the capital-spending cycle.
questions.source: Private investment nearly doubled its pace to close at 12%, and lending grew at its fastest in over a decade.

questions.prompt: In September 2026, Japan Credit Rating Agency (JCRA) raised India's sovereign credit rating to A- from BBB+. Consider the following statements:
items: It was India's first sovereign credit rating upgrade since May 2025.
JCRA is one of the Big Three agencies whose ratings price India's foreign borrowing.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: It was India's fourth upgrade since May 2025, after Morningstar DBRS, S&P Global Ratings and R&I. The Big Three that price India's foreign borrowing are S&P, Moody's and Fitch, not JCRA.
questions.source: It is India’s fourth sovereign credit rating upgrade since May 2025, following Morningstar DBRS, S&P Global Ratings, and Japan's Rating and Investment Information (R&I).

questions.prompt: In September 2026, India notified the full rulebook for Semicon 2.0, funding six pillars of the chip value chain. Which one of the following is NOT among those six pillars?
questions.explain: The six pillars are design, materials, fabrication, packaging, research and talent; device assembly is not one of them. The shift into design and equipment targets the choke points where export controls bite.
questions.source: India notified the full rulebook for Semicon 2.0, funding all six pillars of the chip value chain: design, materials, fabrication, packaging, research, and talent.
